## PR review — system-design

**Used**: Cloned PR 7 at head. Read diff.go, fetch.go, github.go, the board.go and opened_on.go call sites, and the actions.go change. Did not build or run it.
**Standards**: No standards cited. I ran no `standards search`.
**Findings**: 2 correctness · 0 design · 0 prose

### Correctness

**system-design.1** `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:107` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:236` · `internal/pullrequests/fetch.go:41` · `internal/board/board.go:119` · `internal/pullrequests/pullrequest.go:158`

Reach: A user with a checked-out repo opens the board. The provider listing lands and `Prefetch` runs on every refresh. `claim` marks every listed non-merged PR with a checkout as due. The goroutine then runs `git fetch --force origin <head>:refs/remotes/origin/pr/N` and `git fetch origin <base>` in the user's working repo, four PRs at a time. This happens with no keypress, so the user can be mid-rebase or mid-`git fetch` in that repo. Every head, including others' fork PRs through `pull/N/head`, is downloaded. Before this change, `d` did the fetch on one PR, by explicit request. If the remote is ssh with a passphrase and no agent, ssh prompts on /dev/tty. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` covers only https credential prompts. A background prompt then writes into the TUI's terminal. The in-process `checkoutLock` does not guard against the user's own git or a second `prs` process, so ref-lock failures show up as diff faults.

The diff section turns an on-demand, user-triggered fetch into an automatic background write to every checkout the board lists. Each listing refresh also moves `origin/<base>` in the user's repo without being asked.

The size check does not prevent this. `claim` skips the fetch only when the row already carries `Additions` and `Deletions` above the limit. Otherwise it fetches first and counts afterwards.

Fix, either of these:
- Fetch on demand: when the PR's document opens, or when the user presses a key.
- Add an opt-in config flag for prefetch, and set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` with `-o BatchMode=yes` in `run` for these calls.

In both cases, route checkout diffs through a bare scratch clone or `git fetch --no-write-fetch-head` into a private namespace. That leaves the user's `origin/<base>` alone.

**system-design.2** `internal/pullrequests/github.go:334` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:259`

Reach: A GitHub PR is not in a local checkout, or is merged. Its row carries no `Additions` or `Deletions`, or counts below the limit. `readGitHubDiff` calls GET repos/{slug}/pulls/{n} with `Accept: application/vnd.github.diff`. GitHub answers 406 (diff too large) once a diff passes 300 files or 20,000 lines. That error becomes a Fault, and `claim` retries it on every listing refresh because `entry.fault != ""`. With many such PRs, each refresh makes one REST call per failing PR, against the shared REST rate limit that the GraphQL listings also draw from.

A failed read is never remembered for the same head and base. Fix: record the fault together with the `at` key and retry only when `at` changes or after a backoff. Treat a 406 as the terminal 'too large' result, `Whole=false`. Do not treat it as a transient fault.

## PR review — stale-prose

**Used**: I cloned PR 7 at 7d8516d and read every prose line the diff adds. That covered CLAUDE.md, README.md, the help text in cmd/prs/tui.go and cmd/prs/config.go, and the comments in internal/pullrequests/diff.go, fetch.go, github.go and provider.go, internal/board/document.go, internal/board/opened_on.go and internal/config/config.go. I built the binary into my own directory and ran `prs tui --help` with XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME pointed inside my directory. I checked each sentence that states behavior against `diffRoute`, `claim`, `diffAt` and `documentSections`.
**Standards**: I applied two rules. One is pull-requests.md/Sentences the diff adds are checked for what goes stale, and the finding carries the rewrite. The other is documentation.md/A count, version or measurement pinned in a comment or doc names what made it true and how it was measured, or goes stale as a constant, which I found with `standards search "default value written in docs goes stale"`.
**Findings**: 0 correctness · 0 design · 3 prose

### Prose

**stale-prose.1** `cmd/prs/tui.go:58` · `README.md:136`

**False: two sentences say one route serves every pull request, but `diffRoute` sends some elsewhere or refuses them.**

- `cmd/prs/tui.go:58`, in `prs tui --help`: "Each open pull request's diff is read once the list lands: in its checkout, where its head is fetched into refs/remotes/origin/pr/<number> as d fetches it, and from GitHub where its repo is not cloned here."
  - The built binary's `prs tui --help` prints this sentence word for word.
  - At the head, `diffRoute` (internal/pullrequests/diff.go) reads from the host only where `provider.Diff != nil`. That holds for GitHub alone.
  - An uncloned Bitbucket pull request is not read from anywhere. It gets the `Cannot` sentence "prs diffs a pull request on bitbucket only in its checkout…".
  - The help text says that pull request is read from GitHub.
  - Rewrite: "Each open pull request's diff is read once the list lands. Where its repo is cloned here, prs fetches its head into refs/remotes/origin/pr/<number> as d fetches it, and diffs it there. Where it is not, the host sends the diff, and a host whose client has no diff gets a section saying why."
- `README.md:136`: "Bitbucket's client reads no more than its listing, so a Bitbucket pull request's document holds its description and its diff."
  - The "so" no longer follows. The listing-only client explains why the Checks, Files and Comments sections are missing.
  - It does not explain where the diff comes from, which is the checkout, not the client.
  - Rewrite: "Bitbucket's client reads no more than its listing, so a Bitbucket pull request's document has no Checks, Files or Comments." The paragraph below it already says how its Diff is read.

**stale-prose.2** `README.md:129`

**A value the code holds: README.md writes out the default cap.**

- `README.md:129`: "A pull request changing more lines than `diff_section_max_lines` in the config, 300 by default, gets its size and the key that opens it instead."
- The number 300 belongs to `config.DefaultDiffSectionMaxLines` (internal/config/config.go:69).
- The `prs config path` help in this same diff fills it in with `%[2]d`, so it stays level with the constant.
- The README copy goes wrong at the next change to the constant.
- documentation.md § "A count, version or measurement pinned in a comment or doc names what made it true and how it was measured, or goes stale as a constant" also reaches it.
- Rewrite: "A pull request changing more lines than `diff_section_max_lines` in the config gets its size and the key that opens it instead. `prs config path` names its default."

**stale-prose.3** `README.md:133`

**False by omission: the README names one re-read trigger, but `claim` uses four.**

- `README.md:133`: "Each open pull request's diff is read once the list lands, a few at a time, and again when its head commit moves."
- `claim` re-reads when `diffAt` changes. That value is the head commit *and the base*, or the update time where a row names no head.
- `claim` also re-reads when the last read failed (`entry.fault != ""`).
- A reader of the README would expect a pull request retargeted to a new base to keep its old diff, but `claim` reads it again.
- The `Diffs` doc comment in diff.go already lists every trigger correctly.
- Rewrite: "Each open pull request's diff is read once the list lands, a few at a time. It is read again when its head commit or base moves, or when its last read failed."

## PR review — code-architecture

**Used**: I cloned the repo and checked out PR 7 detached. I read `diff.go`, `fetch.go`, `detail.go`, `actions.go`, `document.go`, `rows.go`, `opened_on.go`, `board.go`, `github.go`, `provider.go` and `config.go` at the head. I traced every site that decides a pull request's checkout, base, head and diff range. I compared the new `Diffs` cache with `Details`. I did not build or run anything.
**Standards**: code-quality.md § "Ask whatever owns a fact, the function or enum that computes it, never duplicate its logic at a second site". code-quality.md § "A duplicated implementation copies the originals failure order, not only its result".
**Findings**: 0 correctness · 2 design · 0 prose

### Design and architecture

**code-architecture.1** `internal/board/actions.go:120` · `internal/board/actions.go:127` · `internal/board/actions.go:136` · `internal/board/actions.go:154` · `internal/board/actions.go:428` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:197` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:217` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:267` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:269` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:277` · `internal/board/document.go:242`

Reach: The next change to how a pull request is diffed locally must edit two code paths in step: `d` in `board.diff` and the Diff section in `diffInCheckout` and `diffRoute`. Example changes are a stacked-base rule, a different ref namespace or a new provider whose listing reports no base. The PR itself is that change for one case. It moved the fetch into `Fetch` but left the checkout, base, head and range around it duplicated. `document.go:242` is a third site. It reads `diffRoute`'s choice to name `d` as the key that opens the diff, but `d` gates on `checkoutOf` instead.

### `d` and the Diff section each decide on their own how a pull request is diffed in its checkout

`Fetch` is now shared. Everything around it is decided twice:

- **Is it checked out?** `board.checkoutOf` (actions.go:428) decides this for `d`. `pullrequests.checkedOut` (diff.go:217) decides it for the Diff section. The two predicates are the same and written twice.
- **The base.** `d` uses `pr.Base`, falling back to `defaultBranch(checkout)` (actions.go:127). `diffInCheckout` refuses an empty `pr.Base` (diff.go:269). Bitbucket's `Base` comes from `toRef.displayId`/`destination.branch.name`, so the rules differ for the same row.
- **The head.** `provider.Head(pr)` and the refusal text "names no source branch to fetch" are copied at actions.go:136 and diff.go:267.
- **The range.** `"origin/"+base+"..."+got.Ref` is built at actions.go:154 and diff.go:277.
- **Which key opens the diff.** `opener` (document.go:242) names `d` only where `diffRoute` set `InCheckout`. `diffRoute` also excludes merged pull requests. `d` refuses only on `checkoutOf`. So the document and the key answer "can `d` open this?" by different rules.

This is what code-quality.md § "Ask whatever owns a fact, the function or enum that computes it, never duplicate its logic at a second site" forbids.

**Fix:** one function in `pullrequests` resolves a pull request to its local diff. It returns the checkout, base, head and three-dot range, or the reason it cannot. A name like `LocalDiffTarget(pr) (target, error)` fits. It takes the `defaultBranch` fallback with it. `board.diff`, `diffInCheckout` and `diffRoute` call it. `Fetch` takes the target. `opener` asks the same function, or `d`'s own precondition, rather than reading `InCheckout`.

**code-architecture.2** `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:107` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:131` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:168` · `internal/pullrequests/detail.go:139` · `internal/pullrequests/detail.go:165` · `internal/pullrequests/detail.go:197` · `internal/board/opened_on.go:48` · `internal/board/opened_on.go:58` · `internal/board/rows.go:357`

Reach: The next background read per pull request, such as checks or review threads read separately, will copy a third Prefetch/claim/store/drop loop. It will also have to pick one of two existing rules for keeping the `--pr` pull request alive. This PR is the second instance of the pattern, and its drop rule already differs from the first.

### `Diffs` copies `Details`' cache machinery, and the two keep the `--pr` pull request alive by different rules

`Diffs` and `Details` each carry their own copy of the same loop:

- a mutex and a map by `Key()`
- `Prefetch`, with a slot channel of 4
- `claim`, which marks entries as reading and deletes entries from the same lister that the listing left out
- `store`, which keeps the old value on a failed read
- an `Of` that returns a `Held`/`Reading`/`Fault` state

The two copies have already drifted:

- **Who owns an entry.** `Details` keys its drop on the provider's name. `Diffs` keys it on a free string, `from`.
- **Keeping the `--pr` pull request.** `Details` falls back to the launch read's detail at draw time (`rows.go:357`, `openedOnDetail`). `Diffs` registers a pseudo-lister, `openedOnRead = "--pr"` (opened_on.go:58), so no provider's listing deletes the entry.
- **Completion.** `Details.Prefetch` returns a done channel. `Diffs.Prefetch` returns nothing.

The parts that really differ are small:

- the staleness key: `current` for details, `diffAt` for diffs
- the settle-without-reading cases: `diffRoute` and the line cap
- the read function

**Fix:** pull the loop into one generic cache in `pullrequests`, for example `background[T]`. It takes:

- a lister name
- a staleness key per pull request
- an optional settle-now hook
- a read function

It owns slots, claim, drop and store. Pick one rule for the `--pr` pull request in that cache, either the pseudo-lister or the draw-time fallback, and use it for both caches. `Details` and `Diffs` then each hold only their key, settle and read functions.

**failure-paths.1** `internal/pullrequests/fetch.go:44` · `internal/pullrequests/fetch.go:46`

Reach: Triggered by a checkout whose origin hangs, such as a stalled VPN or a git server that accepts the connection and sends nothing. Prefetch queues one Fetch per due pull request in that checkout. Each holds the lock through up to four git calls, and each call can take readTimeout (2m, pullrequest.go:131). Ten pull requests could hold the lock for tens of minutes. Pressing `d` on a row in that checkout takes the same lock. Traced from the code, not run.

**`Fetch` waits for its checkout lock without honouring ctx, so one hung remote blocks `d` for every queued read.**

`lock.Lock()` cannot be cancelled. A `d` press shows "fetching …" and cannot be cancelled while it waits behind the background diff reads. The user sees a stuck board with no error. When the lock is finally taken, the cancelled ctx fails the first git call. Prefetch also stops nothing after the first timeout, so every queued read of the checkout still waits its own timeout.

Fix: take the lock through a ctx-aware primitive, a `chan struct{}` of size 1 selected against `ctx.Done()`. Return `ctx.Err()` when the wait is cancelled. Better, stop queueing a checkout's remaining reads once one fetch has timed out. Let a user action (`d`) jump ahead of the background reads.

**failure-paths.2** `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:144` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:197` · `internal/pullrequests/provider.go:106`

Reach: Triggered by a Bitbucket pull request that is declined or open with its source branch deleted, in a repo that is cloned. diffRoute sends it to the checkout because standing is not Merged. Bitbucket's Head is pr.Branch, so `git fetch origin <branch>:<ref>` fails. The cause is traced from the code, not run.

**A permanent fetch failure is retried on every listing and shown as a fault, with no stop and no fallback.**

The entry keeps `fault != ""`. The condition at diff.go:144 therefore re-claims it on every `Prefetch`. Each time it re-runs the failing git fetch while holding the checkout lock, which delays the other diffs in that checkout. The Diff section reads "Could not read it: could not fetch #N …" for as long as the branch is gone.

**contracts.1** `internal/pullrequests/fetch.go:11` · `internal/pullrequests/fetch.go:43` · `internal/pullrequests/diff.go:272` · `cmd/prs/tui.go:114` · `datapointchris/dotfiles:apps/common/tmux-sessions`

The tui then runs `git fetch --force origin <head>:refs/remotes/origin/pr/<n>` and `git fetch origin <base>` in every registry checkout that has an open pull request. Any other process fetching into the same repository can collide with it. Worktree sessions count, because they share the primary checkout's refs. That makes the next change cost a cross-process lock. ### A new background writer of every checkout's git refs is locked only inside prs

Before this PR, only `d` wrote into a checkout's refs. It ran one fetch, on a key press. Now `prs tui` fetches each open pull request's head and its base in its checkout as soon as the list lands, and again when the head moves. That is several fetches for each repo on every start. The `fetch origin <base>` call also moves `refs/remotes/origin/<base>`. Worktree sessions read that ref and fetch it themselves, for example to rebase before landing on main.

Either one now races a fetch the person never asked for. The loser is the other program, not prs. data.md § "A state file written by more than one process is changed under a file lock, re-read inside the lock" says it directly: "An in-process mutex covers one process."

- Have the background read fetch only the head refspec, and skip `fetch origin <base>`. Diff against the `origin/<base>` already present, or read from the host when it is missing. Then the background never writes a ref another program reads.
- Or take git's own lock discipline across processes, for example `flock` on `<git-common-dir>/prs-fetch.lock`, and retry once when git fails to lock a ref.
- Or make the background fetch opt-in with a config key, so `d` stays the only writer by default.

The PR body's "What changes" names the `pr/<number>` refs. It never says the base ref moves too, and it should.

Once the list lands, `prs tui` runs `git fetch` in every cloned repo for each open pull request under the cap. `run` sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. The ssh stand-in, reparented, kept reading the terminal and kept git's stderr pipe open. `run` uses `.Output()` with no `WaitDelay`, so `Wait` never returned. With a stand-in that also prompts on `ssh -G`, whose stderr git discards, `Run` did return at the timeout. A failed read is read again on every refresh, so a new prompting ssh started each minute and the orphans piled up.

2. In `run`, give the child no controlling terminal: `SysProcAttr{Setsid: true}`, so ssh fails at once instead of prompting. Kill the process group on cancel, and set `cmd.WaitDelay`. This also covers `d`'s fetch, which has had the same exposure since before this branch.
